title: Run Plex at home? Hackers are exploiting old Plex servers - update tonight
description:
Run Plex at home? Hackers are breaking into old Plex servers.

Plex2Shell is a chain of four flaws in Plex Media Server (CVE-2026-96652, CVE-2026-96654, CVE-2026-96655, CVE-2026-96656). The researcher who found them says that, chained together, they let an attacker run code on the server. On October 20, 2026, the US agency CISA added all four to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

On November 6, QNAP said some customers' Plex servers on its NAS devices appear compromised, and that hacked servers have been used to run cryptocurrency miners and proxy software. Updating alone does not remove what attackers installed. QNAP's own operating systems are not affected; the flaws are in Plex Media Server.

Analyst note: a media server is still a computer on your home network, so patch it like one.

Do this tonight:
1. Update Plex Media Server to 1.43.3.10861 or later, then check the version in Plex Web: Settings, then General.
2. Turn off Plex Remote Access if you don't use it, and don't forward port 32400. Need remote access? Use a VPN.
3. If an old version was reachable from the internet, treat the device as possibly compromised: reset your Plex and device passwords and follow your vendor's clean-up guide.
